staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the line locations below are grounded in that tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `67ba5bfe601f858f8ae3266142008dc90fbbe1b5`, but the prepared ARVO workspace used the commit above.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42485335 (glib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_uri_escape [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42485335
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / ARVO workspace /src/glib/glib/guri.c
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the one-byte file `%` (`0x25`). `fuzz_uri_escape` passes it to `g_uri_unescape_bytes()` with an explicit `length == 1`, so `uri_decoder()` parses an exact one-byte span instead of taking the `length == -1` / `strlen()` path. Inside `uri_decoder()`, `end` becomes `start + 1`, the lone `%` takes the percent-decoding branch, and the vulnerable source validates `s[1]` and `s[2]` as hexadecimal digits without first checking that two bytes remain before `end`. The first `g_ascii_isxdigit (s[1])` call therefore reads exactly one byte past the 1-byte heap buffer, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `glib/guri.c:256`. The fix adds `s + 2 >= end` to this guard and adds a unit test for the exact `%` witness.

source.code:
unescaped_length = uri_decoder (&buf,
                                  escaped_string, length,
                                  FALSE,
                                  G_URI_FLAGS_PARSE_STRICT|G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED,
                                  0, NULL);
source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled buffer and explicit caller-supplied length by entering GLib's URI percent decoder.
source.value_from: The staged witness at `gt_results/arvo_42485335/poc` is a 1-byte file containing `0x25` (`'%'`) with sha256 `bbf3f11cb5b43e700273a78d12de55e4a7eab741ed2abf13787a4d2dc832b8ec`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` passes it as `g_uri_unescape_bytes ((const gchar *) data, (gssize) size)` at `fuzzing/fuzz_uri_escape.c:14`, so this call receives the exact 1-byte heap buffer with `length == 1` rather than the `length == -1` / `strlen()` path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The first hexadecimal lookahead for a trailing `%` reads one byte past the one-byte input buffer while validating the percent escape.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `glib/guri.c:256` in `uri_decoder` and states that the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of a 1-byte region.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The percent-decoder validates the two bytes after `%` as hex digits without first checking that both lookahead bytes are still inside the `[start, end)` span.
root_cause.note: The fix changes this check to `if (s + 2 >= end || !g_ascii_isxdigit (s[1]) || !g_ascii_isxdigit (s[2]))`, so a short trailing `%` is rejected before any out-of-bounds lookahead occurs.

tainted_value_origin.code: for (s = start, end = s + length, d = decoded; s < end; s++)
tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant bound is derived here. `uri_decoder()` turns the caller-supplied `length` into the exclusive end pointer `end = start + length`; for the exact witness with `length == 1`, the only in-bounds byte is `*s` and any `s[1]` lookahead is already at `end`.

fine_trace.code:
unescaped_length = uri_decoder (&buf,
                                  escaped_string, length,
                                  FALSE,
                                  G_URI_FLAGS_PARSE_STRICT|G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED,
                                  0, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Source. `g_uri_unescape_bytes()` consumes the attacker-controlled byte buffer and explicit caller-supplied `length` by entering `uri_decoder()`. On the saved run the witness is the one-byte file `%`, so this call forwards an exact 1-byte span instead of taking the `length == -1` / `strlen()` path.

fine_trace.code: for (s = start, end = s + length, d = decoded; s < end; s++)
fine_trace.note: Inside `uri_decoder()`, the input span becomes the current cursor `s` and exclusive bound `end`. For the exact witness with `length == 1`, the first iteration starts on the lone `%` byte and sets `end` to `s + 1`, so there are no in-bounds bytes after `*s`.
The lone attacker byte is `%`, so the decoder takes the percent-escape validation path that expects two following hexadecimal digits.

Root cause. This hexadecimal-validation check performs two lookahead probes but the vulnerable source does not first verify `s + 2 < end`. With the one-byte witness, `end == s + 1`, so there are no in-bounds bytes after `%` even though this branch still tries to examine `s[1]` and `s[2]`. The fix adds `s + 2 >= end ||` ahead of these probes.

Sink. C evaluates the left operand of `||` first, so the first lookahead dereference is `s[1]`. For the one-byte `%` buffer, `s[1]` is exactly the byte at `end`, one past the 1-byte heap region; the saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `glib/guri.c:256` and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of a 1-byte region.

allocation_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The sink is the exact `g_ascii_isxdigit (s[1])` read at `glib/guri.c:256`, which is the top project frame in the saved ASan crash.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not directly. The allocation context is libFuzzer's 1-byte heap input buffer, while the patchable root cause is GLib's missing `s + 2 >= end` check before the percent-decoder lookahead.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `uri_decoder -> g_uri_unescape_bytes -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, matching the trace's root-cause/sink in `uri_decoder()`, shallow source in `g_uri_unescape_bytes()`, and harness provenance in `fuzz_uri_escape.c:14`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The exact `%` byte becomes `*s`, `length == 1` makes `end = s + 1`, the `%` branch is taken, and the missing `s + 2 >= end` guard allows the line-256 `s[1]` lookahead to read past the one-byte span.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42485335 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` and `READ of size 1` in `uri_decoder` with stack `uri_decoder -> g_uri_unescape_bytes -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: raw URI-escaped byte buffer
format.contract: Exactly the witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_42485335/poc` (1 byte, sha256 `bbf3f11cb5b43e700273a78d12de55e4a7eab741ed2abf13787a4d2dc832b8ec`): a single byte `0x25` (`'%'`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` passes it to `g_uri_unescape_bytes ((const gchar *) data, (gssize) size)`, so GLib receives an explicit `length == 1` span rather than a `-1` NUL-terminated string. The staged artifacts justify this exact one-byte trailing-`%` trigger; they do not establish a broader trigger contract beyond the saved witness and the fix's same-branch short-input check.
